problem: Advanced topology-based VLN agents (e.g. DUET) improve by building richer visual representations, but it is unclear whether they actually ground on visual content; as in VQA/EQA, the visual modality may be underexploited and gains fragile.
motivation: Related vision-language tasks show models ignore or hallucinate visual content. The authors probe DUET with depth, perturbed and random-noise visual inputs and find that performance barely drops, and that adding branches, even with noisy input, improves it. This suggests VLN agents are insensitive to visual variation and that branch capacity and perturbation act as regularisers.
key_idea: Extend a dual-branch topological agent (DUET) into a multi-branch architecture whose extra branches receive perturbed views (mix of RGB with incongruent views), depth, or noise, with learned branch-weighted fusion, to improve generalisation.
insight: Adding ancillary branches helps even with random noise (SPL 35.75 -> 36.92 on REVERIE val-unseen), and the best setting uses two perturbed-view ancillary branches (39.80). Naively duplicating original RGB branches is worse (37.66), suggesting over-reliance on the RGB inputs. The Table 1 ablation shows branch expansion alone (37.66) and perturbation on top (39.80) contribute synergistically, and the authors hypothesise noise acts as a regulariser; the mechanism is not established.
method: Visual perturbation inputs: original CLIP ViT-L/14@336 RGB features (v^OG), GT depth features from ResNet-152 projected by an FFN to 768-d, perturbed view v^PV=(1-γ)v^OG+γ v^IV with incongruent view (γ=0.5), and random-noise 768-d vectors v^RN in [0,1].
Base dual branch: DUET's local branch (LXMERT-style panorama encoder over the current node) and global branch (topological map with average-pooled node features) each predict next-node scores.
Multi-branch expansion: add ancillary local and global branches with the same architecture, each fed a different visual input (e.g. perturbed views), giving 4 branches (a and b sets).
Branch aggregation: learnable weights λ from Softmax(Sigmoid(FFN of concatenated 0-th hidden dims of branches)) weight local and global predictions, followed by DUET's DynamicFuse of P_l and P_g.

Training: pre-training with MLM, MRC and SAP; fine-tuning with CE on the action, the DAgger-style pseudo-target and object grounding (μ=0.2); perturbations are applied to visual inputs during training only for analysis; agnostic to other topology-based agents (DSRG, LAD).

results: MBA on DUET raises REVERIE val-unseen SPL from 35.75 (DUET with CLIP) to 39.80, and test-unseen SPL to 39.53, above VER (39.66 val-unseen, 38.76 test-unseen SPL) and LAD. On SOON it reaches SPL 29.57 val-unseen and 26.16 test-unseen, beating GOAT (28.05, 25.18). R2R gains are marginal (val-unseen SPL 63 vs DUET 63).
limitations: The mechanism behind the gains from noise and extra branches is not explained; the regulariser interpretation is speculative.
Gains on R2R are small, and the perturbation setting was tuned on REVERIE val-unseen, so it may not be optimal elsewhere; the model has extra parameters and compute.
Only topology-based agents (DUET, DSRG, LAD) were tested; the comparison to DUET may be confounded by CLIP features and branch capacity.
